Permission rules and hook matchers match the canonical name only" — so `TaskStop` must be the string that a permission rule, a hook matcher and a subagent tool list all match, and the deny/ask unknown-tool startup warning must NOT fire for it.
current: Our Pi harness spells the tool `stopTask` on every permission-visible axis. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:262` is `binding('stop_task', 'stop_task', 'stopTask', 'stopTask')` — the factory at :219-236 defaults `permissionName = handlerName`, so descriptorId/piName are `stop_task` and bindingName/handlerName/permissionName are `stopTask`. The 5th `binding()` argument, which every documented-name tool uses (`binding('read','read','read','read','Read')` at :247, `sessionBinding('enter_worktree','EnterWorktree')` at :309), is left unused here. `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES` (:351-353) is `[...new Set(PI_TOOL_BINDINGS.flatMap(b => [b.permissionName, b.descriptorId]))]`, so neither projection can yield `TaskStop`. Measured on HEAD with `bun -e`: `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES.includes('TaskStop') === false` (control: `'EnterWorktree'` is `true`), and `parseClaudeRuleString('TaskStop','deny',{knownToolNames:PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES})` returns a rule of `{kind:'tool',semanticId:'TaskStop'}` PLUS `warning.code === 'claude_rule.unknown_tool'` (control: `'EnterWorktree'` returns no warning). Both gate sites miss: `permission-dsl.ts:648` matches a `kind:'tool'` rule against `request.semanticId` (`stop_task`) and `request.toolName` (permissionName, `stopTask`); the removal matcher `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:936-938`) is broader — semanticId, permissionName, bindingName, piName — but that set is still `{stop_task, stopTask, stopTask, stop_task}`. Hooks miss too: `pi-agent.ts:3683` sets `toolName = manifestTool.binding.permissionName` and that value is what rides `tool_name` into `PreToolUse` (`pi-agent.ts:3857`), `PermissionRequest` (`:4322`) and `PostToolUse` (`:3591`), so a hook matcher written `TaskStop` never fires. The three PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES consumers all pass the list unmapped — `permissions-config.ts:529` (Claude `settings.json` import), `managed-policy.ts:1017` (managed tier), `pi-agent.ts:3032` (hook-supplied `updatedPermissions`) — and no normalizer sits above them. The ONE place `TaskStop` already resolves is subagent/skill tool lists: `runtime-agent-definition.ts:94-95` carries `taskstop: ['stopTask','stop_task']` in `PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES`, consumed only by `normalizePiRuntimeAgentToolName` (:106-114). The Claude SDK backend is not affected — `TaskStop` is the SDK's own name there (`packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:136`).
divergence: Value right, key name wrong, on one binding. The tool exists, is reachable and behaves correctly; only the string a permission rule / hook matcher must write is ours (`stopTask`, Pi's upstream tool name from `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:648`) instead of the documented one (`TaskStop`). Two of the three axes tools-reference.md:9 names are wrong (permission rules, hook matchers); the third (subagent tool lists) is already right via the alias table. Because `TaskStop` is absent from `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES` the mismatch is not merely silent: `managed-policy.ts:1034-1037` REFUSES any managed rule that raises `claude_rule.unknown_tool`, so an admin's `deny: ["TaskStop"]` is stripped from the policy entirely, and the Claude-settings importer (`permissions-config.ts:540`) installs a rule that matches nothing while logging the warning only to `debug()`. This is the same shape as the already-reasoned `Glob`→`Find` case (`claude-permission-rules.test.ts:245-247`), but with the opposite answer: `Find` is a deliberate product rename, whereas `stopTask` is the SAME tool under a non-documented spelling, and the file's own rule at `harness-tool-descriptor.ts:303-309` says the permissionName must be the documented spelling verbatim.

blastRadius: Crosses BOTH a wire boundary and a persistence boundary — a risk trigger under this repo's rules, so the boundary set must be proven once on the final diff. (1) WIRE: `binding.permissionName` rides the Pi execution manifest into the subprocess and is echoed back on every pre-tool request; `pi-agent.ts:3684-3687` throws `Pi pre-tool identity mismatch` if host and subprocess disagree. Both sides import the same `@nessy-agent/shared` constant so they move together, but a mixed-version host/subprocess pair would hard-fail every stopTask call. (2) PERSISTENCE: rule strings are stored verbatim in settings files by the `applyPermissionRequestUpdates` write path (`pi-agent.ts:3005-3050`); an already-persisted `stopTask` deny would stop matching. Nothing user-facing ever documented that spelling, so real exposure is near zero. (3) Rule consumers of PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES: `permissions-config.ts:529`, `managed-policy.ts:1017` (which STRIPS unknown-tool rules at :1034), `pi-agent.ts:3032`. (4) Gate and removal: `permission-dsl.ts:648`, `:936-938`, and the EndConversation guard at `:984` (all four identity spellings). (5) Hook payloads: `pi-agent.ts:3591`, `:3857`, `:4322` now carry `tool_name: 'TaskStop'`; plugin hook matchers and stored automations keyed on `stopTask` would stop matching (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts:182` `EXTERNAL_HOOK_TOOL_NAMES` maps only `bash → Bash` today). (6) TRANSCRIPT/UI: `agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:1053-1061` sets the displayed `toolName` from permissionName, so the tool renders as `TaskStop` instead of `stopTask` — intended, and it matches `packages/ui/src/components/chat/task-checklist.ts:21`, which already reasons in `TaskStop` terms. (7) Skill grants: `agent/core/prerequisite-manager.ts:76` builds `PERMISSION_NAME_BY_TOOL` values from permissionName and `:375` compiles a skill's `allowed-tools` entry through it; `core/__tests__/skill-tool-grant-subject.test.ts` pins the map against the bindings. (8) MODEL-CONTRACT PIN: `pi-agent-server/src/harness/tool-manifest.ts:300-317` folds permissionName into `presentationReplacements`, which rewrites projected prompt text feeding `hashProjectedPiToolDefinition` (:365-379) and thus `PI_STATIC_MODEL_CONTRACT_HASHES.stopTask`. `grep -a TaskStop` finds the string in no Pi tool description or promptSnippet, so the pin should be unchanged — but it must be re-verified, not assumed: run `packages/pi-agent-server/src/harness/live-manifest-contract.test.ts`, `.../harness/tool-manifest.test.ts` and `.../__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts`. (9) NOT affected: the Claude SDK backend (`agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:136` already lists `TaskStop` as an SDK built-in) and `runtime-agent-definitions.test.ts:392`, which already pins `['TaskStop','stopTask']`.
userImpact: Observable, but narrow and only on the Pi backend. Today a user who follows Claude's docs and puts `"deny": ["TaskStop"]` (or `"ask"`) in a `.claude/settings.json` we import gets a rule that installs and matches nothing: the tool is neither removed from the model's context nor gated, so the agent can still abort the user's background subagents and workflows despite the deny, and the mismatch warning goes only to `debug()` — there is no surfaced startup warning to catch it. On the managed/admin tier the failure is louder and the opposite direction: `managed-policy.ts:1034-1037` refuses any rule raising `claude_rule.unknown_tool`, so an administrator's `deny TaskStop` is stripped from the policy at load and reported as dropped. Third, a plugin or settings hook whose `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` matcher is `TaskStop` never fires on this tool, because the payload's `tool_name` is `stopTask`. Fourth and cosmetic: the transcript labels the call `stopTask`, a name that appears in no documentation the user can read. What makes it narrow is that nobody would guess `stopTask` on their own, so today the only way to write a working rule is to read our source — the documented spelling is the one that fails.
